object_description: compact six-level volume organized around patios
design_condition: Located at the western end of the site, the compact building creates a large esplanade but turns its main entrance away from the principal student flows and remains weakly connected to the adjacent course.

positive.statement: The composition of the first two levels is interesting, with open spaces and a mezzanine bringing together key public functions.
The staggered alternation of the four patios provides nice spatial variety.
The corridors benefit from quality lighting and visual clearances.
The structure is simple and rational.

negative.statement: The main entrance turns its back on the main flows of students coming from the station and city center.
The staging of the gymnasiums on two gallery levels seems excessive for their primary purpose.
Independent access to the sports halls lacks quality and has small dimensions.
Arranging classes on four levels is not optimal and reaches the limit of the required comfort.
The large glazing of the aula and gymnasiums struggles to convince in its use and architectural integration.
The vast esplanade does not interact sufficiently with the main course, leaving the two spaces juxtaposed.
